title: NASA InSight — instruments and evidence
note: This explorer summarizes published mission and instrument facts. The diagram is an original schematic, not a photograph or a reconstruction of telemetry.

instruments.name: SEIS
instruments.role: Listen to the inside of Mars
instruments.question: What can marsquakes and impacts reveal about the planet’s interior?
instruments.description: A seismometer placed directly on the Martian surface measured vibrations from marsquakes, meteorite impacts, and environmental activity. A wind and thermal shield helped protect it.
instruments.outcome: SEIS returned seismic observations that helped scientists investigate the crust, mantle, and core of Mars.

instruments.name: HP³
instruments.fullName: Heat Flow and Physical Properties Package
instruments.question: How much heat escapes from the inside of Mars?
instruments.description: HP³ was designed to use a self-hammering probe nicknamed the mole to travel into the ground and measure heat flow. Unexpected soil properties prevented it from reaching its planned depth.
instruments.outcome: The mole did not reach its intended depth. That engineering difficulty also taught researchers about the unexpected properties of Martian soil.

instruments.name: RISE
instruments.question: What does Mars’ tiny wobble tell us about its core?
instruments.description: RISE used radio tracking between Earth and the lander to measure tiny changes in the position of Mars’ rotation axis. Those measurements help scientists infer the size and composition of the planet’s core.
facts: Up to one hour per day
instruments.outcome: Radio-tracking measurements helped refine estimates of Mars’ interior, including information about its core.
